boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Minnesota-Twin Cities, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-stakes, under-21-friendly first-weekend route through campus landmarks, study spaces, arts, and student resources.

cards.title: Start with the Goldy Gopher Statue
cards.subtitle: Outside Coffman Memorial Union
cards.notes: Meet your new people at the bronze statue, take a quick group photo, then use Coffman as the anchor for the rest of your East Bank walk.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable campus meeting point and photo stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the six-foot-tall Goldy Gopher statue was unveiled outside Coffman Union in 2013.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor statue outside Coffman Memorial Union.

cards.title: Get Oriented at Coffman Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: 300 Washington Avenue SE
cards.notes: Use the building directory to find the U Card Office, Great Hall, food options, and student resources before splitting off to explore nearby campus.
cards.short_summary: A central union with services, food, and gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Coffman Memorial Union's official directory lists the U Card Office, Great Hall, Goldy's Gameroom, and multiple dining locations.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: Check the union's current building-hours page before visiting; U Card access may be required outside public hours.

cards.entity_name: University of Minnesota Bookstores at Coffman Memorial Union
cards.title: Browse the Coffman Bookstore
cards.subtitle: Ground level of Coffman Memorial Union
cards.notes: Take a no-rush lap through the general and academic titles, supplies, and campus merchandise; buy only what you actually need for the term.
cards.short_summary: A campus bookstore inside Coffman with books, supplies, and Gopher items.
cards.evidence_claim: The official bookstore page places the store on Coffman Union's ground level and lists books, course materials, supplies, and University merchandise.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | U of M Bookstores
cards.access_notes: Located at 300 Washington Ave SE; confirm current store hours on the official page.

cards.title: Walk Across Northrop Mall
cards.subtitle: East Bank campus green
cards.notes: Walk the mall slowly and point out the buildings you will recognize later; pause on the grass or paths for a simple campus-orientation reset.
cards.short_summary: A signature East Bank green framed by major campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The University's campus-visit page specifically identifies studying in the grass of Northrop Mall as part of the Minneapolis campus experience.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor mall; access and conditions vary with weather and campus operations.

cards.title: Look Inside Northrop
cards.subtitle: Northrop Mall
cards.notes: Check the events calendar for a performance, talk, film, or workshop, and find a study lounge if you want a calm indoor place to regroup.
cards.short_summary: A campus venue for performances, talks, films, and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Northrop says students gather there for performances, lectures, concerts, film screenings, ceremonies, and other activities; it also has student study lounges.
cards.access_notes: Event entry and prices vary. Consult Northrop's current calendar and event page before attending.

cards.title: Settle into Walter Library
cards.subtitle: East Bank
cards.notes: Find a seat for a brief planning session: compare schedules, make a course-material list, and bookmark library help before your first full week begins.
cards.short_summary: A historic East Bank library and practical first-week study stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Walter Library opened as the University's main library in 1924 and is documented by the University Libraries as a Roman Renaissance-style building.
cards.source_title: Walter Library building history | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access campus libraries; consult the Libraries' current hours before going.

cards.title: See the Weisman Art Museum
cards.subtitle: 333 East River Road
cards.notes: Choose one gallery or exhibition to explore at your own pace, then step outside to notice the building and river-facing campus setting.
cards.short_summary: A university art museum with free gallery admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Weisman Art Museum states that admission is always free and that everyone is welcome.
cards.access_notes: Verify current gallery hours and any event registration requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Cross the Washington Avenue Bridge
cards.subtitle: Between East Bank and West Bank
cards.notes: Walk across in daylight with your group, pause only where pedestrian traffic stays clear, and use the crossing to get a first look at the river corridor.
cards.short_summary: A pedestrian connection between East Bank and the West Bank arts district.
cards.evidence_claim: The University's campus-visit information describes crossing the Mississippi River to reach West Bank and taking in river and natural-park views from the Washington Avenue Bridge.
cards.access_notes: Use designated pedestrian routes and be mindful of weather, bicycles, and other bridge users.

cards.title: Check Out the Recreation and Wellness Center
cards.subtitle: 123 SE Harvard Street
cards.notes: Stop by to orient yourself to the fitness, climbing, court, and lounge options; save a class or activity idea for a later visit with your U Card.
cards.short_summary: A large East Bank recreation facility with fitness and activity spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: RecWell identifies its East Bank facility at 123 SE Harvard St and lists fitness centers, climbing and bouldering walls, courts, gymnasiums, and an esports lab.
cards.access_notes: Facility access depends on membership; fee-paying students have automatic membership with a valid U Card.

cards.title: Plan a St. Paul Campus Visit to the Bell Museum
cards.subtitle: 2088 Larpenteur Avenue West, St. Paul
cards.notes: Save this for a daytime outing: explore the natural-history exhibits, planetarium offerings, and outdoor learning landscape, then check transit or shuttle details first.
cards.short_summary: A St. Paul campus natural-history museum and planetarium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bell Museum describes itself as Minnesota's official natural history museum and planetarium on the University of Minnesota Twin Cities campus in Saint Paul.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Tuesday-Sunday hours; admission prices and planetarium availability should be checked before visiting.
